comments.mergedPostDetails:
1. Go to a world with someone on live and you on the beta.

2. Switch to this avatar : https://vrchat.com/home/avatar/avtr_afa9d203-c185-4eb1-8933-b37eb75ae711

3. In your expressions toggle "Combat"

4. Do a fingerpoint gesture with both hands and make both fingers touch

5. With both fingers now on fire, lift them both high up above your head

6. Game crashes for players in the beta instead of playing the phase2 transition properly
comments.mergedPostTitle: Some particle setups makes the beta crash when in a world with people on unity 2019 and others on 2022
comments.value:
For reference, it's an avatar I made. I've deduced it's from two animations, a "dash" mechanic and a fire snap effect, both of which use "buffer particles" to use the same particle system (in an attempt to optimize). My theory is that with how buffer particles change between Unity 2019 and Unity 2022, the engine can't quite figure out what's going on and instantly closes the game. I'm really not sure why it would work in older versions of Unity and not newer ones, though.

Here's what I mean by "Buffer Particles":

https://twitter.com/hfcRedddd/status/1696913583928455652
Hello!  Thanks for reporting this.  A number have updates have gone out since this post, could you confirm this issue is still occurring?

@{5d298c00339ddf69186a0453|full_name}: Hi! Do you have an avatar ID that reproduces the crashing? Can be a private avatar as well.

@{62b61f8ec938a62475e4cd14|full_name}: Yep! ID is as follows: 

avtr_afa9d203-c185-4eb1-8933-b37eb75ae711.

It's a public avatar named "Cynthia‚ Radiant Fury v1․06 FINAL" if that doesn't work.

For the crash to occur, you'll need to enter your radial menu and enable "Combat". From here, hold Point with both of your controllers, bring your hands together (this will spawn two fireballs which I believe will cause a crash), then raise both of your hands above your head. It'll spawn a large pillar of fire around you if you don't crash. From here, if you're still in-game, you can use your left hand fist and then fingergun in rapid succession to snap. There's a 5 second cooldown between successful snaps, but both the fireballs in the "phase-up" and the snap have been found to cause the crash.

Friends I've tested this with have reported the game literally just closes instantaneously. No warning, no freeze, it's like someone hit the X button on the application.

I have another public avatar with the ID of

avtr_3a96e532-d5bd-4925-a92b-ab55a1d0b45e 

named "Gideon, Lightning God v1.17" that uses the same principle for identical lightning strikes between multiple animations (as a refresher, to cut down on particle systems and materials), and also was discovered to cause identical unintended crashes.

details:
1. Launch VRChat

2. Load Avatar

3. Activate an animation that uses Buffer Particles (basically emitters that have their subemitters removed from their parents. I use them to re-use a common particle system to optimize a bit)

4. If on the Unity 2022 Beta, remote users who see the animation instantly crash with no warning. As in, the game instantly closes.

This was not done intentionally and frankly I am appalled my avatar has become a crasher unwillingly. I'll do whatever I can to mitigate the issue in the meantime. It's likely something to do with how the behavior of Buffer Particles change between Unity 2019 and 2022. 

Attached is a Twitter thread by HFCRed explaining the differences and how to "fix" Buffer Particles - problem is, my Buffer Particles are already set up like in the thread.

https://twitter.com/hfcRedddd/status/1696913583928455652
